help.intro: A brand is a name and a slug, plus one content entry per language. The slug is what identifies it, and it is scoped to the brand type rather than global.
help.step_1_title: Name it and set the slug
help.step_1_body: The slug is trimmed and lower-cased on save, so casing and stray spaces are not yours to control. It must be unique for the brand type — saving a duplicate is refused outright rather than corrected.
help.step_2_body: Type is half of the uniqueness key, so the same slug can exist once per type. Only "product" exists today, which means slugs are effectively unique overall for now.
help.step_3_title: Write the content, one language at a time
help.step_3_body: At least one language entry is required, and each language may appear only once — a repeated language is rejected, not merged. Description and meta are optional within an entry.
help.step_4_body: Brands are active or inactive and move freely between the two. There is no draft or pending state.
help.step_5_title: Add a logo and set the order
help.step_5_body: Images opens the logo slot — a brand carries one logo, not a gallery. Order arranges every brand of one type at once, and is what sorting by order then reads.
help.note: Deleting a brand is a soft delete, and the uniqueness rule ignores deleted rows — so the slug becomes free immediately and can be taken by a new brand. Restoring the old one then fails while that name is in use.
